name: fossel-repo-memory-v1
description: Repo-memory retrieval eval for a fictional e-commerce codebase (acme/storefront). 45 memories, 33 labelled queries. Query categories are chosen to be fair rather than flattering: 'exact', 'identifier', 'path' and 'ticket' are cases keyword search should win outright, 'paraphrase' and 'synonym' are cases keyword search should lose, 'multi' checks multi-answer recall, and 'superseded' plants an outdated memory as a distractor that outranks the current one lexically. Memory array order is recency order (first entry is newest); rarely-queried memories are placed first on purpose so the recent-memory backfill in get_context cannot inflate scores by luck.

memories.note: Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and the release job derives the next version from them.
Feature branches are named feat/<ticket>-<slug> and squash-merged into main.
Unit tests live next to the file under test as *.test.ts, not in a separate top-level tests directory.
Do not add barrel re-export files; import from the concrete module path instead.
Store all timestamps in UTC and convert to local time only in the render layer.
New user-facing features ship behind a flag in flags.ts and default to off.
Fixed a cart race condition by making the addToCart mutation idempotent on the client-generated line id.
Checkout froze on Safari 16 because of a nested form element; fixed by hoisting the submit button out.
We chose Postgres over DynamoDB for the order store because the reporting queries need joins.
We chose the Next.js App Router over Remix; the deciding factor was the existing Vercel deployment.
Structured logs go to stdout as JSON; the collector attaches trace ids, so do not log them yourself.
Before the 3.2 release the session JWT was kept in localStorage.
styled-components was the styling system until the 4.0 refactor.
Use pnpm workspaces for all package scripts; npm and yarn lockfiles are rejected by CI.
Lint and format with Biome before pushing; there is no ESLint or Prettier config in this repo.
All environment variables must be declared in env.schema.ts and are validated at boot.
Monetary amounts are persisted as integer minor units, never as floating point values.
The session JWT is kept in an httpOnly cookie named sf_session and never in localStorage.
A 401 response from the API triggers a redirect to /login with the current path in the next query param.
Access tokens live 15 minutes and are renewed by the silent refresh worker in refreshWorker.ts.
Permission checks go through canAccess() in src/auth/rbac.ts; never read the role claim directly.
Public API routes are mounted under /api/v2; /api/v1 is frozen and receives security fixes only.
List endpoints use cursor pagination with an opaque cursor, not limit and offset.
POST /api/v2/orders requires an Idempotency-Key header and replays the stored response on a repeat.
Rate limiting is enforced at the edge worker, so the local development server applies no limits at all.
Run pnpm db:migrate before starting the dev server after pulling main.
Schema migrations must stay backwards compatible for one release so a rollback never needs a down migration.
Analytics queries must target the read replica via withReplica(), not the primary connection.
The Stripe webhook handler was processing events twice; fixed by storing the event id and rejecting replays.
Fixed a memory leak in the product gallery caused by an unremoved resize listener in useGallery.
Product search missed accented names until we normalized to NFD and stripped diacritics before indexing.
Order dates rendered one day early for users behind UTC because the value was formatted from a UTC string.
Resolved an N+1 query on the order history page by batching line item loads through a dataloader.
Issue #412 tracks the flaky checkout e2e test that fails when the seeded fixture clock crosses midnight.
Issue #587: the CSV export truncates at 10000 rows and needs to stream instead.
JIRA-2291 covers migrating the legacy admin panel off AngularJS.
We decided not to split the monolith into microservices until the team passes 25 engineers.
Tailwind is the only styling system; styled-components was removed in the 4.0 refactor.
Reviewers expect pull requests under 400 changed lines; larger ones get split before review starts.
Reviewers require a failing test in the same commit as any bug fix.
Reviewers ask for before and after screenshots on any UI change.
Deploys go out through the release workflow on tag push; nobody ships from a laptop.
Rollback is a redeploy of the previous tag, not a revert commit on main.
The on-call engineer owns the alert channel for the whole week and hands off at Monday standup.
Secrets are injected from the platform secret store at runtime; .env files are for local development only.

queries.rationale: Literal term match; FTS should win outright.
Single rare token; tests that a one-word query still works.
camelCase symbol; embeddings cannot help, tokenization must.
Path tokenization; two memories legitimately mention it.
The canonical hybrid-search motivating case: zero token overlap with any auth memory.

queries.query: how are prices represented in the database?
what should I do before starting the dev server after a git pull?
are there limits on how many requests I can make locally?
how big can a code review be?
why is this still one deployable unit?
dates showing up wrong for some customers
why was the order history slow?
search cannot find products with accented characters
what happens when a deploy goes wrong?
queries.rationale: Requires connecting 'goes wrong' to 'rollback'. Hard for lexical and for hashed embeddings alike; included to show the ceiling honestly.

queries.query: can I put a password in a file in the repo?
where is the session JWT stored?
queries.rationale: m-oldjwt is an outdated memory that shares more surface terms with the query than the current answer does. A retriever that ignores recency will rank the wrong one first.
